text: The Northern Lights are the Sun's wind crashing into our sky.
The Sun blows out a stream of tiny charged bits.
We call it the solar wind.
Earth's magnetic field pushes most of it away.
But it steers some of it down toward the poles.
There, about a hundred kilometers up, the bits slam into the air.
Oxygen glows green. Higher up, it glows red.
So every curtain of light is the Sun's wind, lighting up our air.
